items.q: Who can apply?
a: Anyone aged 18 or over with a startup idea. You can be at any stage: just an idea, validating the problem, building a prototype, live with early users, or already earning revenue.

items.q: What do I need to bring?
a: The idea. FutureAcad forms the team around you through StartupVarsity, so you don't need co-founders or engineers before you apply.

items.q: Which industries can I choose?
a: AI and deep tech, BFSI and fintech, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, and logistics and mobility.

items.q: What should I write in the application?
a: What problem you are solving, for whom, and why you are the right person to solve it. Also tell us what you have built or led before, and share your LinkedIn or portfolio.

items.q: What happens after I apply?
a: Interview calls go out within two weeks of applying. Applications for Cohort 1 are open now.

items.q: Is my idea kept private?
a: Yes. FutureAcad does not share applications with third parties, and uses your details only to contact you about StartupVarsity.

items.q: What does StartupVarsity give a founder?
a: A six-month programme with an 11-member team of AI-native engineers, ₹10 lakh in seed funding and access to more than 100 mentors. The idea and the company are yours to lead.

items.q: Do I need a technical background?
a: No. Tell us what you have built or led before, in any field. The team brings the engineering skills, and FutureAcad engineers guide the build.

items.q: How does the interview work?
a: We talk about your idea, the problem you want to solve and the customers you want to serve. Then we agree whether StartupVarsity is the right next step for you.

items.q: Who is this for?
a: AI-native freshers who are ready to build inside a funded startup team. You must be 18 or over.

items.q: Which roles are open?
a: AI and ML engineering, full-stack development, data and analytics, cloud and DevOps, product and design, and business and growth.

items.q: Is the internship paid?
a: Yes. The stipend is ₹10,000 to ₹25,000 a month, depending on the role.

items.q: Which industries can I work in?
a: Retail and e-commerce, manufacturing or the public sector. If you are not sure yet, choose "Not sure yet" and we will help you decide.

items.q: What should I include in my application?
a: Your graduation year, a link to your LinkedIn, GitHub or portfolio, the role you want, and three things about you: your skills, your projects and your interests.

items.q: What happens to my details?
a: FutureAcad uses them only to contact you about StartupVarsity, and does not share applications with third parties.

items.q: What will I actually do?
a: You join a funded startup team for six months and build a real product with its founder, guided by FutureAcad engineers and mentors. You ship real work, not practice tasks.

items.q: Do I need work experience?
a: No. This is for freshers. Show us your skills, the projects you have built and what you want to learn. A strong GitHub or portfolio helps.

items.q: What comes after the internship?
a: You leave with real projects to show employers, and with experience of building inside a startup team from day one.

items.q: Which teams are hiring?
a: FutureAcad is growing across LEARN, BUILD and TRANSFORM, and many of these roles are entirely new. We welcome seasoned technologists, educators, partnerships professionals and early-career professionals.

items.q: How do I apply?
a: Email info@futureacad.ae with your CV, and tell us which pillar interests you: LEARN, BUILD, TRANSFORM or PARTNER. We reply within a week.

items.q: What tools will I work with?
a: An AI-native stack, including Claude, Cursor and other modern AI tools, in a culture that values shipping over showing.

items.q: I'm a student or a founder. Is there a way in for me?
a: Yes. Join a StartupVarsity team, either as a founder with an idea or as an intern who wants to build.

items.q: What is a micro GCC, and can FutureAcad set one up in India?
a: A micro GCC is a small, dedicated India team that works like your own centre, without the cost of a full captive set-up. FutureAcad's pods are micro GCCs: Pod-S is a tech lead and two AI/ML or full-stack engineers, Pod-M has 6 and Pod-L 12, all badged to you. Start with one pod, scale to 50+ engineers, and take ownership through Build–Operate–Transfer.

items.q: What is the build operate transfer model?
a: Build–Operate–Transfer (BOT) is a model where a partner builds a team or centre for you, runs it for an agreed period, and then hands ownership to you.

With FutureAcad, the build and operate phases run for 24–36 months under your brand and governance. At the end, the team, the entity, the office and the IP transfer to you, on terms fixed when you sign. You can start small, with a 6-month trial pod, before committing to the full model.

items.q: Should a Bengaluru mid-sized company build an in-house GCC team or use a staffing partner with managed engineering pods?
a: If you have not yet proven the model, use managed pods first. An in-house GCC means a local entity, leased space and a leadership team, and takes 12–18 months before first code. A managed pod from FutureAcad starts with 3–6 engineers on a monthly bill and aims for a first production ship 8 weeks from a signed SoW. Because Build–Operate–Transfer is in the contract, you can still end up owning the centre.

items.q: What should a startup look for in a GCC-as-a-Service provider with a build-operate-transfer option?
a: Judge providers on five things: a small trial with an exit clause, dedicated pods with a named lead, evidenced compliance, trained engineers from day one, and fixed transfer terms. FutureAcad has a hub in Bengaluru (plus Dubai and Singapore), a 6-month trial pod, and Build–Operate–Transfer over 24–36 months.

items.q: How big is a starter pod, and how does it grow?
a: Pod-S is 3 engineers, Pod-M is 6 and Pod-L is 12. You can add pods each quarter, and the model scales from 3 to 50+ engineers. FutureAcad handles hiring, payroll, infrastructure, attrition and the bench.

items.q: What do I own at the end of a Build–Operate–Transfer?
a: FutureAcad builds and runs your centre under your brand and governance for 24–36 months, then transfers the team, the entity, the office and the IP to you. Transfer terms are fixed at signing.

items.q: How fast can a pod ship something?
a: Week 0 is a 30-minute pod sizing call. Weeks 1–2 cover pod composition and the SoW. Weeks 3–4 cover activation in your tools and security policies. Weeks 5–8 deliver the first production ship.

items.q: Can I hire the engineers onto my own payroll instead?
a: Yes. With Hire-Train-Deploy you choose from a pool of 1.3M+ trained engineers, FutureAcad trains to your spec, and you hire. The fee is charged only on placement.

items.q: Can FutureAcad help us set up a GCC in India?
a: Yes. FutureAcad sets up and runs your GCC in India as GCC-as-a-Service: a 30-minute pod sizing call, pod composition and the SoW, activation in your tools, and a first production ship by week 8. Build–Operate–Transfer is in every contract.

items.q: Are you GCC setup consultants, or do you run the team too?
a: Both. FutureAcad advises on the set-up, then hires, trains and runs the team under your brand, and transfers the team, entity, office and IP to you when you are ready.

items.q: Who can help set up a GCC in India?
a: FutureAcad helps companies set up a new GCC in India as GCC setup consultants and operators: we hire the team, run it, and transfer it to you. If you are comparing companies that help set up a GCC in India, the key questions are who hires, who runs it, and what you own at the end.

a: In a build-operate-transfer arrangement in India, the company starts with a small pod, we run it for a set period, and then the team and processes transfer to the client's own capability centre. Ask us which examples we can share.
